sources.name: d042-beta-doe-primary
sources.locator: First two explanatory paragraphs distinguishing beta-minus from beta-plus.
facts: In beta-minus decay a neutron becomes a proton while an electron and an antineutrino are emitted.
Beta-plus decay instead converts a proton to a neutron with positron and neutrino emission.
The emitted beta electron is not evidence for a stored nuclear electron.
exclusions: The source133 negative-electron equation is not a rule for all beta decay.
Do not add a neutrino symbol to the retained equation without the equation-change contract.
No experimental statistics, health claim or neutrino research digression is imported.

sources.name: d042-tritium-epa-primary
sources.locator: Header half-life table and first descriptive paragraph.
facts: Tritium is a hydrogen isotope with one proton and two neutrons.
It emits beta particles; EPA lists a half-life of12.3years.
The printed approximation of about12years is consistent with rounding, rather than an exact half-life.
exclusions: The more precise number is evidence only; no new visible quantity is authorized.
Environmental exposure, medical effects, disposal rules and isotope applications are not imported.
This source does not verify the printed deuterium abundance or heavy-water phase-transition values.
